lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Coastal Marine Services | Diesel Mechanic | Lake City, USA | Jul 2025 - Present
- Rebuilt diesel engines and gearboxes for a fleet of 14 commercial fishing vessels, keeping dry-dock time under 5 days per job.
- Maintained hydraulic winch systems and logged service records for the harbor authority's annual inspections.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Owned the weekly carrier scorecards for the regional managers and the monthly review meeting that discussed them.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.

- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots while rewriting the standard operating procedures, running driver training and taking over vendor negotiations for the telematics contract, which saved 1,800 driver hours a year across the region.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
- Lifted checkout conversion from 61% to 66% by testing a one-page flow against the three-step flow across 40,000 sessions, then shipping it to all merchants.
- Prioritized the dispute roadmap with RICE, scoring Reach as the number of support tickets each feature would close.
- After interviewing 25 merchants, mapping chargeback reasons, sizing the loss by segment and drafting a business case with finance, set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran the checkout A/B test with randomization by session and reported the 5-point conversion lift as the effect on merchants' customers.
- Presented the onboarding results and a follow-up roadmap to the payments leadership team, who funded the rollout to two more regions.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Raised weekly active users from 400 to 1,150, a 150% increase, by adding pickup reminders chosen after 60 user interviews.
- Raised the pickup-slot fill rate by 20% across two dining halls, from 75% to 95%, by setting up a volunteer shift system.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Sized a $2.4M annual saving from consolidating outpatient scheduling across 4 clinics; the client funded a pilot based on the model.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Presented the final recommendation to the hospital COO and clinic directors, who approved a 90-day scheduling pilot at two clinics.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: The resume does not establish one clear product, product-operations, or operations-strategy narrative.
items.because: The experience currently presents several possible professional identities equally and makes the recruiter infer the target role.

items.says: The emphasis should be tailored for each target career path rather than using one version for all roles.
items.because: Different roles require Harbor Payments, Crestline, or other experience to receive greater emphasis.

items.says: Education should lead only for entry-level or MBA-targeted roles; otherwise experience should come first.
items.because: Section order should reflect the strongest evidence for the target role.

items.says: The Coastal Marine Services entry should take less space unless the target role values field operations or industrial systems.
items.because: The mechanic role should not compete with the product narrative.

items.says: Crestline Logistics should receive more emphasis than the mechanic role.
items.because: It is stronger evidence for product operations, operations strategy, and analytical roles.

items.says: The Harbor Payments section should put the strongest product outcome first and group related work together.
items.because: The current organization makes its strongest evidence less clear.

items.says: Six overlapping bullets make the short Harbor Payments internship look inflated.
items.because: Repetition may cause readers to question how much work was independently owned.

items.says: For product applications, the Campus Food Rescue project could appear before Coastal Marine Services.
items.because: The project is more relevant to product work than the current mechanic role.

items.says: The consulting-practicum bullets should be organized around the strongest business outcome.
items.because: The current bullets overlap, particularly around pilot approval.

items.says: A specific summary could connect the MBA, economics, operations, analytics, experimentation, and user research to the target role.
items.because: The varied background currently requires explanation to avoid appearing unrelated.

items.says: Metrics throughout the resume need more precise baselines, periods, scope, attribution, and definitions.
items.because: Precision problems can undermine otherwise strong metric-rich achievements.

items.says: Punctuation and line wrapping should be standardized.
Add a clear target-position descriptor near the name or contact information.
items.because: The header currently gives no indication of professional focus despite experience spanning mechanics, logistics, product, and consulting.

items.says: The LinkedIn URL appears to be a placeholder or generic website rather than an actual LinkedIn profile.
items.because: The displayed address is example.com/in/riley-chen.

items.says: Consider adding location or work authorization when relevant to the target roles.
The MBA's completed or ongoing status should be stated explicitly.
items.because: A date range without a completion indicator creates unnecessary uncertainty.

items.says: Add a relevant concentration, course, leadership role, award, or distinction only if it is genuinely strong.
items.because: The MBA should support the product or operations transition narrative rather than stand alone as a credential.

items.says: The degree location could be removed if space is needed.
items.because: The economics degree is no longer the primary selling point compared with the professional experience.

items.says: The current diesel-mechanic role needs context explaining why it belongs in a product or operations application.
items.because: Recruiters may interpret a mechanic role after an MBA as a change away from product or business work.

items.says: The scale and personal ownership of the engine and gearbox work are unclear.
items.because: The bullet does not define the volume or boundaries of the work.

items.says: The operational significance of keeping dry-dock time under five days is unclear.
items.because: The reader cannot tell whether five days is an improvement, a required standard, or the normal duration.

items.says: It should be confirmed that under five days was repeatable performance rather than an isolated best case.
The bullet needs clearer business impact through turnaround, reliability, safety, downtime, or similar context.
items.because: Mechanical work is not naturally connected to product or business operations.

items.says: The bullet may not be worth keeping for product-focused applications.
items.because: It is less relevant than nearly every other bullet on the resume.

items.says: The maintenance tasks should be reframed around operational, compliance, asset-management, or documentation impact.
items.because: As written, the bullet is primarily a responsibility statement.

items.says: Add scale or consequence such as systems maintained, inspection outcomes, uptime, or avoided disruption.
items.because: The bullet shows no measurable result, decision, improvement, or scope.

items.says: Add the scale of the carrier scorecards, such as carriers, regions, shipments, managers, or metrics.
items.because: The current bullet does not establish the scope of the responsibility.

items.says: Clarify what decisions or business changes resulted from the scorecards and review meeting.
items.because: Responsibility for reporting does not show the value it enabled.

items.says: State whether the reporting process was built, improved, or merely administered.
items.because: The current wording reads as administrative rather than analytical ownership and decision influence.

items.says: Add the baseline or operational consequence of the 30% error reduction.
items.because: Error volume, customer impact, labor cost, or returns would make the scale more credible.

items.says: Clarify the role performed relative to the floor supervisors.
items.because: It is unclear whether the contribution covered analysis, design, implementation, training, or all four.

items.says: Specify the period over which the 30% reduction was measured.
items.because: A percentage reduction is more credible with measurement context.

items.says: Make the forecast's size and business importance clearer.
items.because: The current bullet does not establish the scale of the planning process.

items.says: Clarify whether the consensus method was created or its adoption was facilitated.
items.because: The distinction between originating, coordinating, and operationalizing the method affects ownership.

items.says: Specify the forecast horizon or error metric definition for analytically rigorous readers.
Separate or clarify the implementation, change-management, training, and vendor-management responsibilities.
items.because: Several achievements in one long sentence can obscure the strongest result.

items.says: Explain how the 1,800 annual driver-hour saving was calculated.
items.because: The quantified claim will receive scrutiny.

items.says: Clarify the level of ownership in the vendor negotiation.
items.because: The boundaries between operational work and commercial negotiation should be clear.

items.says: Translate the saved hours into cost, capacity, or service impact if possible.
items.because: Financial or operational consequences would make the result more meaningful.

items.says: Clarify the personal contribution to the onboarding redesign.
items.because: The bullet does not distinguish discovery, requirements, workflow design, coordination, experimentation, and launch ownership.

items.says: Confirm that the time reduction was measured against a comparable pre-launch cohort.
items.because: The bullet currently attributes the full improvement to the redesign.

items.says: The causal attribution between the redesign and the entire time-to-payment reduction needs measurement support.
items.because: The current wording implies that the redesign caused all of the improvement.

items.says: Consider including activation, support-volume, or retention impact if those outcomes were affected.
items.because: Those dimensions may be more valuable than additional process detail.

items.says: Clarify whether the conversion change is five percentage points or a relative percentage increase.
items.because: Product and growth readers will probe the interpretation of the metric.

items.says: State whether the A/B-test result was statistically significant if that information is available.
items.because: The test's statistical and measurement details need precision.

items.says: Clarify whether all merchants means the pilot region or the company's entire merchant base.
items.because: The rollout scope is ambiguous.

items.says: Do not imply that the post-test rollout produced the same conversion result unless it was measured.
items.because: The experiment and subsequent full rollout are different scopes.

items.says: The RICE bullet needs the decision or outcome produced by the prioritization.
items.because: It currently shows familiarity with a framework rather than product judgment.

items.says: Add the number of features, stakeholders, or roadmap choices involved.
items.because: The current bullet does not show the scale of the prioritization work.

items.says: Clarify whether the RICE model was adapted or simply applied.
items.because: The level of judgment and ownership is unclear.

items.says: Explain that defining Reach as support tickets closed was an intentional company-specific choice.
items.because: Otherwise it may look like a misunderstanding of the framework.

items.says: Distinguish this roadmap bullet more clearly from the preceding RICE bullet.
items.because: Both bullets currently describe roadmap prioritization.

items.says: Clarify the intern's decision authority and the role of the product manager or team.
items.because: Set the next quarter's roadmap priority may sound too senior or absolute for an intern.

items.says: Add the resulting business outcome, such as expected loss reduction, approved investment, or a shipped feature.
items.because: The bullet ends with prioritization rather than its impact.

items.says: Make the link between customer research, analysis, and the roadmap choice explicit.
items.because: The sequence of evidence and decision is not fully clear.

items.says: Remove or consolidate this bullet with the earlier checkout-conversion bullet.
items.because: It largely duplicates the same experiment without adding a new business result.

items.says: Check the unit of analysis and interpretation of the reported effect.
items.because: The technical detail may invite methodological questions.

items.says: Clarify whether session-level randomization created repeat-user or exposure concerns.
items.because: Randomizing by session may affect how the customer-level result can be interpreted.

items.says: Clarify whether the presentation was delivered independently or as part of a team.
items.because: Personal ownership is not defined.

items.says: Identify exactly what the leadership approval enabled.
items.because: The organizational consequence should be explicit.

items.says: Verify that funded accurately describes the leadership decision.
items.because: If leadership only approved rollout without allocating budget, the wording is too expansive.

items.says: Clarify whether the app was a live university partnership, student venture, or volunteer-run service.
items.because: Recruiters need to understand the project's legitimacy and operating context.

items.says: State whether the app was built personally, by a team, or by an external developer.
items.because: The heading does not establish the scope of product ownership.

items.says: Clarify whether 3,100 students means the addressable audience, registered users, or users reached.
items.because: The reader cannot tell whether the product actually served 3,100 users.

items.says: Explain the personal role in launch and adoption.
items.because: The bullet does not define individual ownership.

items.says: Support the claim that nine tonnes of food would otherwise have been discarded with tracking methodology.
items.because: The food-waste counterfactual needs verification.

items.says: Mention the type of partner or stakeholder involvement if applicable.
items.because: The operating context may have depended on university or dining-hall partners.

items.says: The stated 150% increase should be verified.
items.because: The percentage calculation needs precision.

items.says: Add the period over which weekly active users rose from 400 to 1,150.
items.because: The growth metric lacks time context.

items.says: Clarify whether the interviews directly led to the reminder feature or merely informed it.
items.because: Interviews do not by themselves prove that reminders caused the full increase.

items.says: Confirm that weekly active users were measured consistently before and after the change.
items.because: Consistent measurement is necessary for a credible comparison.

items.says: Calling the move from 75% to 95% a 20% increase is mathematically ambiguous and should be 20 percentage points or about 27% relative.
items.because: Product and analytics readers distinguish percentage-point changes from relative percentage increases.

items.says: Add the time period and number of pickup slots or shifts measured.
items.because: The operational metric lacks scale and measurement context.

items.says: Explain the personal role in designing and implementing the volunteer system.
items.because: Individual ownership is unclear.

items.says: Position the result intentionally as a product outcome, an operations outcome, or both.
items.because: The work extends beyond software features into service operations.

items.says: Clarify whether the $2.4 million figure is modeled, validated, expected, or realized savings.
items.because: The distinction is important for credibility.

items.says: Identify the model's main analytical inputs if space permits.
items.because: The current bullet does not show how the savings estimate was developed.

items.says: Specify whether the model was built personally or by a team that was led.
items.because: Individual analytical ownership is unclear.

items.says: Add a measurable result such as completion time, error reduction, abandonment, or staff hours saved.
items.because: Adopted is a positive but vague outcome.

items.says: Clarify whether the intake-form changes were part of the scheduling recommendation or a separate workstream.
items.because: The relationship to the main practicum project is unclear.

items.says: Explain the personal role in mapping, redesign, and adoption.
items.because: The passive wording does not establish ownership.

items.says: Clarify whether the final recommendation was presented personally or by the full team.
items.because: Individual executive-communication ownership is unclear.

items.says: Avoid duplicating the pilot-approval outcome already reported in the first practicum bullet.
items.because: Two bullets currently prove the same client decision.

items.says: Distinguish methods used directly from methods merely studied.
items.because: Every listed skill should be defensible and supported by the experience above.

items.says: The skills list undersells demonstrated strengths in analytics, implementation, forecasting, process improvement, and cross-functional execution.
items.because: The resume shows broader capabilities than the four listed product skills.

items.says: Clarify the level of ownership behind roadmapping.
items.because: The Harbor bullets leave uncertainty about whether roadmap decisions were made, recommended, or supported.

items.says: The tools list is thin for product and analytics roles.
items.because: Only Jira, Amplitude, and Excel are listed despite the analytical work described elsewhere.

items.says: Show the specific Excel work through experience bullets rather than relying on the generic tool name.
items.because: Excel alone does not communicate proficiency or application.

items.says: Jira and Amplitude need concrete support showing where and how they were used.
items.because: The experience section currently does not substantiate those tool claims.
